latest_nl_proof:
Let d = x - j/n. Since x \ge j/n, subtracting j/n from both sides gives d \ge 0. Also, since x < (j+1)/n = j/n + 1/n, subtracting j/n gives d < 1/n. Hence 0 \le d < 1/n.

By the definition of d, we have x = j/n + d. Since J_{n,j}(d) is defined to be j/n + d, it follows that x = J_{n,j}(d).

This proves the statement.
role_in_parent: Extracts the additive offset coordinate from the interval hypothesis.
statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. If x is a real number with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n and d = x - j/n, then 0 <= d < 1/n and x = J_{n,j}(d), where J_{n,j}(d) = j/n + d.

domain_restrictions: n is a positive integer (so n is nonzero)
j is an integer satisfying 0 <= j <= n - 1
x is a real number satisfying j/n <= x and x < (j + 1)/n
J_{n,j}(d) is evaluated as j/n + d for the given n, j, and real d
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Given n in positive integers, j in integers with 0 <= j <= n - 1, and x in reals with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n, let d be defined by d = x - j/n. Then d satisfies 0 <= d < 1/n, and x equals J_{n,j}(d) where J_{n,j}(d) = j/n + d.

for all real numbers x with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n
